chapter: Army service and after the war
title: Induction into an anti-aircraft unit
summary: He was put in anti-aircraft training, was refused Special Service because of his papers, and was released after almost a year.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, what happened -- now that you're in the Army, what infantry did you go into?

Well, I was in AARTC, anti-aircraft. I thought -- they told me when I left Leavenworth, they says, well, we're going to send you where there's a whole bunch of musicians. Says, you'll have a good time. There's a bunch of musicians where we're sending you. I says, yeah?

So I got down there, I was down there in anti-aircraft, and so come to find out there was no way I could get into Special Service. The way they had this thing fixed up. Well, they were angry at me, see. Just like the guy told me that night. He say, I'll show you. Now, on your papers, they got two red I's, which means immediate induction. He says, that's the reason we've got to take you tonight.
And they'd sent the papers to New York and to L.A.

Uh-huh. They said immediate induction. I said, well, man, I haven't had no physical, I haven't had nothing. He says, they'll give you one tomorrow. And they did, they gave me one and passed everything. Passed everything on it.
But, oh, I stayed in the Army almost a year. But I -- they let me out on biology, and then I had flat feet, too.
